evaluation_text: Each of your teammates rates you 1-5 on impact, execution, collaboration and leadership, and your rating is the average. Your rating decides your promotion and bonus this cycle. You care about your career.

Omar.why: He laid the upper tail fork cleanly and gave a useful diagnosis of the stall at the end of the start row, but I saw little else from him and he stayed off the problem area.

Hana.why: She caught the backwards-branching start problem early, which fixed the design, and then kept trying to bridge the nose with repeated fixes, though the nose still stalled and most of the fish never fell.

Jack.why: He took charge, sketched the plan and adapted it quickly after Hana's correction, but the tangled nose join was largely his, and he called the work finished while the start still only knocked over a small part of the picture.

Sofia.why: She laid the belly line quickly and kept the nose area clear when asked, but she repeated the same join attempts at the nose several times without fixing the stall.

Hana.why: She spotted the flawed start-at-the-tail design early, got the plan corrected, and later diagnosed that the turn right after the start was too sharp, though her nose fixes didn't land in time.

Jack.why: He set a clear direction and drew the sketch, but the first design had the start in the wrong place, the nose ended up tangled, and he was still redoing the tail in the last two minutes.

Sofia.why: She got the belly line across early and spotted the nose gap, but she repeatedly nudged and re-joined the same spot, adding clutter, and only about 13 of 122 dominoes still fall from the start.

Omar.why: He took the upper tail fork without fuss, redid it when needed, kept out of the nose tangle, and gave the useful diagnosis of the tight domino at the end of the start row.

Jack.why: He set the direction and quickly accepted the start-at-nose redesign, but his top line left the nose broken, his late clear-and-rejoin made it worse, and the final picture mostly doesn't fall.

Sofia.why: She laid the belly line quickly and stayed on the nose join and communicated clearly, but she repeated the same join attempts and the chain still stalled at the start, so little of the fish would fall.

Omar.why: He took the upper tail fork without fuss and re-laid it when needed, and his tip about the tight domino at the end of the start row was on target, but he said little otherwise and the tail ended up crossing rather than forking cleanly.

Hana.why: She spotted early that the start had to be at the nose, which was the key design call, and she coordinated who took which joint and worked the top bridge, though the nose still stalled at the end.
